I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day

Negative Appraisals.value: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down

vignette: Kaito's fingers moved deftly over the strings of his guitar, but the music was just a distant hum in his mind. It had been two years since the stalking started, and he still couldn't shake off the feeling of being watched. The memory of that time was fragmented, like shattered glass - some pieces sharp as knives, others dull and inaccessible. He remembered the first note, slipped under his door with no return address, just a single sentence: "I know where you live." The words had seemed laughable then, but soon he was receiving messages every day, each one more menacing than the last. As the weeks went by, Kaito became increasingly withdrawn. He stopped playing gigs at new venues, afraid of unfamiliar places and the dangers they might hold. Even in his own neighborhood, he found himself watching others closely, searching for signs that they might be following him. Nighttime was the worst - he would lie awake, listening for footsteps outside his apartment, his heart racing with every creak of the floorboards. But it wasn't just the present moment that haunted Kaito; the past kept intruding as well. Memories of the stalking would resurface suddenly, without warning - a snippet of a conversation with one of his tormentors, the sound of footsteps outside his door, the feeling of being trapped and helpless. When these fragments appeared, they felt completely real, as if he was reliving the moment all over again. And yet, there were also vast gaps in his memory, moments that simply refused to come into focus no matter how hard he tried. As a musician, Kaito had always been attuned to his emotions, but now he felt numb, like a part of him had been extinguished. He couldn't help but wonder if it was all his fault - if he had somehow brought this on himself through weakness or negligence. The failure of the police and other institutions to stop the stalking only added to his sense of despair. Why hadn't they protected him? Didn't they care? Kaito's divorce from his wife, Linh, had been a quiet one, but it was clear that the stalking had taken its toll on their relationship as well. She had tried to be supportive, but he could see the fear in her eyes whenever he talked about the notes or the messages. Eventually, she couldn't take it anymore and left him. Now, at 50, Kaito feels like a shadow of his former self. He still plays music, but it's just a hobby now - a way to fill the empty hours rather than a source of joy. What finally brought him to seek help was the realization that he couldn't go on living like this - always looking over his shoulder, waiting for the next message or the next attack. He wants to learn how to quiet the constant hum of fear in his mind, how to feel safe again, and maybe even find a way to heal the wounds of the past. But most of all, he's afraid that it may be too late - that the damage has been done, and he'll never be able to reclaim the life he once had.
